concepts.description: The ring of integers (or number ring) corresponding to a number field is the integral closure of ℤ in the number field.

source.docstring:
The ring of integers (or number ring) corresponding to a number field
is the integral closure of ℤ in the number field.

This is defined as its own type, rather than a `Subalgebra`, for performance reasons:
looking for instances of the form `SMul (RingOfIntegers _) (RingOfIntegers _)` makes
much more effective use of the discrimination tree than instances of the form
`SMul (Subtype _) (Subtype _)`.
The drawback is we have to copy over instances manually.
source.note: Exact exported declaration. Import is NOT a local compiler or axiom audit.

source.docstring:
We say that a real number `x` is a Liouville number with exponent `p : ℝ` if there exists a real
number `C` such that for infinitely many denominators `n` there exists a numerator `m` such that
`x ≠ m / n` and `|x - m / n| < C / n ^ p`.

exponent.

source.docstring:
The ramification index of `P` over `p` is the largest exponent `n` such that
`p` is contained in `P^n`.

In particular, if `p` is not contained in `P^n`, then the ramification index is 0.

If there is no largest such `n` (e.g. because `p = ⊥`), then `ramificationIdx` is
defined to be 0.

The Legendre symbol of `a : ℤ` and a prime `p`, `legendreSym p a`,
is an integer defined as

* `0` if `a` is `0` modulo `p`;
* `1` if `a` is a nonzero square modulo `p`
* `-1` otherwise.

Note the order of the arguments! The advantage of the order chosen here is
that `legendreSym p` is a multiplicative function `ℤ → ℤ`.

source.docstring:
The `vonMangoldt` function is the function on natural numbers that returns `log p` if the input can
be expressed as `p^k` for a prime `p`.
In the case when `n` is a prime power, `Nat.minFac` will give the appropriate prime, as it is the
smallest prime factor.

In the `ArithmeticFunction` locale, we have the notation `Λ` for this function.
This is also available in the `ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt` locale, allowing for selective
access to the notation.

concepts.name: BoundingSieve
concepts.statement: Type
concepts.formal_statement: Type
concepts.description: We set up a sieve problem as follows.

source.docstring:
We set up a sieve problem as follows. Take a finite set of natural numbers `A`, whose elements
are weighted by a sequence `a n`. Also take a finite set of primes `P`, represented by a squarefree
natural number. These are the primes that we will sift from our set `A`. Suppose we can approximate
`∑ n ∈ {k ∈ A | d ∣ k}, a n = ν d * X + R d`, where `X` is an approximation to the total size of `A`
and `ν` is a multiplicative arithmetic function such that `0 < ν p < 1` for all primes `p ∣ P`.

Then a sieve-type theorem will give us an upper (or lower) bound on the size of the sifted sum
`∑ n ∈ {k ∈ support | k.Coprime P}, a n`, obtained by removing any elements of `A` that are a
multiple of a prime in `P`.

A primitive Pythagorean triple `x, y, z` is a Pythagorean triple with `x` and `y` coprime.
Such a triple is “primitively classified” if there exist coprime integers `m, n` such that either
* `x = m ^ 2 - n ^ 2` and `y = 2 * m * n`, or
* `x = 2 * m * n` and `y = m ^ 2 - n ^ 2`.

concepts.statement: ℝ → ℕ → ℚ
concepts.formal_statement: ℝ → ℕ → ℚ
concepts.description: We give a direct recursive definition of the convergents of the continued fraction expansion of a real number ξ.

source.docstring:
We give a direct recursive definition of the convergents of the continued fraction
expansion of a real number `ξ`. The main reason for that is that we want to have the
convergents as rational numbers; the versions `(GenContFract.of ξ).convs` and
`(GenContFract.of ξ).convs'` always give something of the same type as `ξ`.
We can then also use dot notation `ξ.convergent n`.
Another minor reason is that this demonstrates that the proof
of Legendre's theorem does not need anything beyond this definition.
We provide a proof that this definition agrees with the other one;
see `Real.convs_eq_convergent`.
(Note that we use the fact that `1/0 = 0` here to make it work for rational `ξ`.)

concepts.name: FermatLastTheoremWith'
concepts.statement: (R : Type u_2) → [inst : CommSemiring R] → ℕ → Prop
concepts.formal_statement: (R : Type u_2) → [inst : CommSemiring R] → ℕ → Prop
concepts.description: A relaxed variant of Fermat's Last Theorem over a given commutative semiring with a specific exponent, allowing nonzero solutions of units and their common multiples. 1.

source.docstring:
A relaxed variant of Fermat's Last Theorem over a given commutative semiring with a specific
exponent, allowing nonzero solutions of units and their common multiples.

1. The variant `FermatLastTheoremWith' R` is weaker than `FermatLastTheoremWith R` in general.
   In particular, it holds trivially for `[Field R]`.
2. This variant is equivalent to the original `FermatLastTheoremWith R` for `R = ℕ` or `ℤ`.
   In general, they are equivalent if there is no solutions of units to the Fermat equation.
3. For a polynomial ring `R = k[X]`, the original `FermatLastTheoremWith R` is false but the weaker
   variant `FermatLastTheoremWith' R` is true. This polynomial variant of Fermat's Last Theorem
   can be shown elementarily using Mason--Stothers theorem.

concepts.statement:

    Algebra.discr K ⇑(IsPrimitiveRoot.powerBasis K hζ).basis =
      (-1) ^ ((↑p ^ k).totient / 2) * ↑↑p ^ (↑p ^ (k - 1) * ((↑p - 1) * k - 1))

      (-1) ^ ((↑p ^ k).totient / 2) * ↑↑p ^ (↑p ^ (k - 1) * ((↑p - 1) * k - 1))
concepts.description: If p is a prime and IsCyclotomicExtension {p ^ k} K L, then the discriminant of hζ.powerBasis K is (-1) ^ ((p ^ k).totient / 2) * p ^ (p ^ (k - 1) * ((p - 1) * k - 1)) if Irreducible (cyclotomic (p ^ k) K)).

concepts.description: Given a positive integer n, ModularCyclotomicCharacter' n is a multiplicative homomorphism from the automorphisms of a field L to (ℤ/dℤ)ˣ, where d is the number of n'th roots of unity in L.

source.docstring:
Given a positive integer `n`, `ModularCyclotomicCharacter' n` is a
multiplicative homomorphism from the automorphisms of a field `L` to `(ℤ/dℤ)ˣ`,
where `d` is the number of `n`'th roots of unity in `L`. It is uniquely
characterised by the property that `g(ζ)=ζ^(ModularCyclotomicCharacter n g)`
for `g` an automorphism of `L` and `ζ` an `n`th root of unity.

concepts.formal_statement: {N : ℕ} → [inst : NeZero N] → (ZMod N → ℂ) → ℂ → ℂ
concepts.description: The completed L-function of a function ZMod N → ℂ, modified by adding multiples of N ^ (-s) / s and N ^ (-s) / (1 - s) to make it entire.

source.docstring:
The completed L-function of a function `ZMod N → ℂ`, modified by adding multiples of `N ^ (-s) / s`
and `N ^ (-s) / (1 - s)` to make it entire.
source.note: Exact exported declaration. Import is NOT a local compiler or axiom audit.

concepts.name: ZMod.differentiableAt_completedLFunction
concepts.statement:
∀ {N : ℕ} [inst : NeZero N] (Φ : ZMod N → ℂ) (s : ℂ),
  s ≠ 0 ∨ Φ 0 = 0 → s ≠ 1 ∨ ∑ j, Φ j = 0 → DifferentiableAt ℂ (ZMod.completedLFunction Φ) s
concepts.formal_statement:
∀ {N : ℕ} [inst : NeZero N] (Φ : ZMod N → ℂ) (s : ℂ),
  s ≠ 0 ∨ Φ 0 = 0 → s ≠ 1 ∨ ∑ j, Φ j = 0 → DifferentiableAt ℂ (ZMod.completedLFunction Φ) s
concepts.description: The completed L-function of a function ZMod N → ℂ is differentiable, with the following exceptions: at s = 1 if ∑ j, Φ j ≠ 0; and at s = 0 if Φ 0 ≠ 0.

source.docstring:
The completed L-function of a function `ZMod N → ℂ` is differentiable, with the following
exceptions: at `s = 1` if `∑ j, Φ j ≠ 0`; and at `s = 0` if `Φ 0 ≠ 0`.
source.note: Exact exported declaration. Import is NOT a local compiler or axiom audit.

concepts.name: ZMod.exists_sq_eq_neg_one_iff
concepts.statement: ∀ {p : ℕ} [inst : Fact (Nat.Prime p)], IsSquare (-1) ↔ p % 4 ≠ 3
concepts.formal_statement: ∀ {p : ℕ} [inst : Fact (Nat.Prime p)], IsSquare (-1) ↔ p % 4 ≠ 3
concepts.description: -1 is a square in ZMod p iff p is not congruent to 3 mod 4.

source.docstring: `-1` is a square in `ZMod p` iff `p` is not congruent to `3` mod `4`.
source.note: Exact exported declaration. Import is NOT a local compiler or axiom audit.

concepts.description: Convert an integer to a ℤ√d

source.docstring: Convert an integer to a `ℤ√d`
source.note: Exact exported declaration. Import is NOT a local compiler or axiom audit.

concepts.name: addWellApproximable
concepts.statement: (A : Type u_1) → [inst : SeminormedAddGroup A] → (ℕ → ℝ) → Set A
concepts.formal_statement: (A : Type u_1) → [inst : SeminormedAddGroup A] → (ℕ → ℝ) → Set A
concepts.description: In a seminormed additive group A, given a sequence of distances δ₁, δ₂, ..., addWellApproximable A δ is the limsup as n → ∞ of the sets approxAddOrderOf A n δₙ.

source.docstring:
In a seminormed additive group `A`, given a sequence of
distances `δ₁, δ₂, ...`, `addWellApproximable A δ` is the limsup as `n → ∞` of the sets
`approxAddOrderOf A n δₙ`. Thus, it is the set of points that lie in infinitely many of the sets
`approxAddOrderOf A n δₙ`.
source.note: Exact exported declaration. Import is NOT a local compiler or axiom audit.
